summary.tldr: Creates a citizenship path for certain former children in care and pauses removal orders for applicants until their citizenship decision is final.
what_it_does: Creates a path to citizenship for some people who were in child welfare or foster care in Canada when that care ended, if they were not citizens then.
Requires applicants to have been physically present in Canada for at least 1,095 days before applying, and to have spent at least 365 days in the listed care situations.
Requires that they were not returned to a parent’s care unless it happened within 365 days after they turned 18, and that they have not lived outside Canada for more than 10 years since then.
Lets the minister waive some of those conditions on compassionate grounds.
Requires the minister to accept an applicant’s written statement about the care circumstances as proof unless the minister proves the statement is wrong.
Stops removal orders from being enforced against foreign nationals who apply under this citizenship rule until a final decision is made.
summary.background: It adds a new section 5.3 to the Citizenship Act and a related rule in the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
